correspondence.component_scope: Head south of Chillar to El Diamante and La Paloma
correspondence.finding: The selected head is in the plain south of Chillar, west of the Route 3 corridor, and continues south through the El Diamante/La Paloma country. Both detailed maps cover the intervening land and isolated depressions. No named source stream or continuous receiving connection from this northern head to La Gogita–La Filomena is established.
correspondence.correspondence: Original geographic coverage read; hydrological connector remains materially unresolved.

correspondence.component_scope: La Gogita–La Filomena–El Pucho and Route 3
correspondence.finding: Farther south, mapped drainage and marshes lead through the La Filomena/El Pucho country, across Route 86 west of Benito Juárez, into the El Cisne/San Eloy wetland setting. The valley then bends southeast through the Route 3 crossing near El Pescado and the Tres Claveles country toward the railway northeast of Alzaga. That southern wetland-to-defined-channel receiving passage is shown. Laguna Oromí, Laguna del Hunco and Laguna San Antonio lie separately to the east of the selected route.
correspondence.correspondence: Original seasonal-wetland and channel correspondence; no perennial-flow requirement or exact bank assignment.

correspondence.component_scope: Arroyo Pescado Castigado through El Ombú and El Chapar
correspondence.finding: The southeastward selected valley is explicitly labeled Pescado Castigado on the original sheets. It passes the El Ombú and La Colina country, Colonia Juan de Garay and El Chapar, then turns east through the San Cala/18 de Marzo setting. Its continuation is again labeled Arroyo El Pescado Castigado south of the separate Arroyo Quequén Grande approach. The two channels are distinguishable on the map.
correspondence.correspondence: Original connected channel and hydronym correspondence.

correspondence.component_scope: Pescado Castigado–Quequén Grande junction and Juan N. Fernández
correspondence.finding: The selected Pescado Castigado valley approaches from the west and joins the mapped Arroyo Quequén Grande continuation in the San Ernesto setting southwest of Juan N. Fernández. The northern approach has the separate Calangueyú and Quequén Grande labels. Downstream the selected course turns south/east past Los Tres Leones, crosses the road setting south of Juan N. Fernández and receives the separately mapped Arroyo Dulce approach. No upstream branch is renamed after the downstream representative candidate.
correspondence.correspondence: Original junction cartography; article prose independently supports the Pescado Castigado to Quequén Grande relationship.

correspondence.component_scope: La Dulce–Lobería lower river and tributary junctions
correspondence.finding: The selected river bends east north of Nicanor Olivera/La Dulce, passing north of Laguna La Salada and Laguna La Dulce Grande rather than traversing those lakes. It continues through the Malal-Tuel/La Gloria setting into the labeled Río Quequén Grande valley. Quequén Chico enters from the north/west side of Lobería, and the Tamangueyú approach joins farther downstream near El Ventarrón. The 1:500,000 original bridges the white missing-content patch in the 1:250,000 mosaic over part of this lower connection.
correspondence.correspondence: Connected lower river and material junctions observed on original maps; smaller map's blank patch resolved by the independent scale layer.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Quequén Grande and actual coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: The river turns south through the La Claudina/El Dominó and La Reserva country, west of Pieres, and continues through the San Lorenzo/Quequén transport crossings. The original 1:500,000 map shows its continuation between Necochea and Quequén into Puerto Quequén and the open coast. The selected terminal is this river-mouth setting, not a nearby coastal lagoon. The 1:250,000 mosaic's terminal blank area is not used as evidence.
correspondence.correspondence: Actual coastal receiving connection observed on the original continuous overview.

correspondence.component_scope: Branches, lakes and drainage character
correspondence.finding: Only one selected mainstem FID is retained. No reservoir passage is shown. Primary field-based research describes a low-gradient Pescado Castigado catchment with seasonal courses, diffuse runoff, ditches and lakes; its defined principal channel discharges into Quequén Grande. This supports reading the upper wetland setting without requiring permanent flow, but does not supply the unresolved northern selected link.
correspondence.correspondence: Original maps plus bounded primary prose; basin association is not substituted for the missing connector.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected mainstem fragment 11506
correspondence.finding: Headward streams east of the Utría coastal ridge turn southeast, then south into the upper Baudó valley. The selected headward approach and its continuation are visible; no separate headwater label is assigned.
correspondence.name_scope: The representative Baudó identity is not propagated to every small headward stream.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Selected mainstem fragment 11507
correspondence.finding: The upper valley continues south into a widening alluvial corridor, reaching the Nauca junction area north of Pie de Pato. The transition into the next selected fragment is visible.
correspondence.name_scope: Bounded upper-valley correspondence; no independent scalar hydronym established for this entire fragment.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Selected mainstem fragment 11508
correspondence.finding: The labelled Baudó corridor passes Pie de Pato, receives lateral Apartadó and Urudó drainage, and continues to the western Dubasa–Catrú lower tributary junction.
correspondence.name_scope: Baudó label supports the main valley. Names of lateral tributaries remain distinct.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Selected mainstem fragment 11509
correspondence.finding: The main valley passes Torreidó and Querá drainage, receives Pepé near Boca de Pepe, turns west, receives Misará, and reaches Bahía Baudó beside Pizarro.
correspondence.name_scope: The main river and coastal terminal support the representative system name. Estuarine branches and adjoining independent coastal rivers are not uniformly named Baudó.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Selected tributary fragment 11510
correspondence.finding: This short selected lower Pepé reach runs west to its actual Baudó confluence near Boca de Pepe.
correspondence.name_scope: Only the selected lower tributary fragment is reviewed; neither its entire upstream basin nor the name Baudó is assigned to it.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Selected tributary fragment 11511
correspondence.finding: A western headward feeder turns north and then southeast into the labelled Dubasa corridor, continuing to the Catrú junction.
correspondence.name_scope: Río Dubasa is directly mapped on the continuing corridor; the initial feeder is not separately named. IIAP uses the spelling Dubaza.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Selected tributary fragment 11512
correspondence.finding: Below the Dubasa–Catrú junction, the combined channel bends southeast and east, receives the Ancosó approach, and joins Baudó.
correspondence.name_scope: The separate Catrú approach is labelled on the map; IIAP identifies Catrú within the Dubaza subbasin. No new compound hydronym or uniform scalar name is assigned to this combined reach.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: headward meseta north of Darwin, Ruca Malén and San Bernardo sector
correspondence.finding: The headward portion is mapped on the meseta north of Darwin and the active Río Negro valley. Several small local depressions and waterbody symbols occur around Ruca Malén and the Laguna San Bernardo vicinity. The selected route is not the mapped Río Negro or its valley channels.
correspondence.correspondence: Original cartography reviewed throughout; dry and non-channel stretches retained as such.
correspondence.name_scope: San Bernardo is a local lagoon label; neither it nor nearby estancia labels supply a river name for this component or the entire feature.

correspondence.component_scope: middle meseta, Las Mercedes–La Reforma–José García and La Larga/La Fortuna/El Mate vicinity
correspondence.finding: The middle route extends east-southeast through mapped meseta relief, crosses the RN22 corridor, and continues past Las Mercedes and La Reforma. Its broad southward and then northward bend lies among local depressions near José García and the separately depicted lagoons La Larga, La Fortuna and El Mate. The source terrain and these waterbodies are readable across the whole interval; no common channel name joins them.
correspondence.correspondence: Whole middle corridor observed in both scales; absence of a continuous named watercourse is an observed naming/feature-scope limitation, not missing map coverage.
correspondence.name_scope: These lagoon labels describe separate local features. No through-flow, successive lake passage or shared river name is assigned to the modeled route.

correspondence.component_scope: lower corridor, El Recado–El Rezongo–El Rosario–La Elba/Lote24 sector
correspondence.finding: The lower selected portion crosses dry relief and local low areas, with a small separately mapped waterbody in the El Rosario/La Argentina vicinity. Terrain continues east-southeast through the La Elba and Lote24 district. A sequence of estancia labels and nearby pans cannot be treated as the name or proof of a single continuous river.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete selected lower interval and intervening terrain observed on the original mosaics.
correspondence.name_scope: Orientation labels only; no whole-route hydronym established.

correspondence.component_scope: actual retained inland terminal, Estancia San Juan/La Dora sector
correspondence.finding: The actual selected endpoint is within inland meseta low terrain in the Estancia San Juan/La Dora sector. Its surrounding relief and small local depressions are visible in the originals; no named receiving waterbody is labeled at the selected endpoint. The mapped Bajo de la Calandria lies separately to the north, and neither the active Río Negro nor Río Colorado is the depicted terminal.
correspondence.correspondence: Actual terminal setting reviewed; no missing terminal map or unresolved unseen recipient is used as a reason for this scope hold.
correspondence.name_scope: No terminal hydronym assigned. The retained endorheic classification remains model metadata; the maps establish inland terrain context without supplying a whole-system name or confirming a modern perennial drainage.

correspondence.component_scope: Headward Somuncurá drainage
correspondence.finding: The original map shows an intermittent headward drainage south of Laguna Blanca, between the Corona/Media Luna and Los Cuatro Cerros sector of the Sierra de Somuncurá, continuing south and then southeast past the Mimbre area. Its connected upper valley continues through the Quiñeluf, Liempe and Loma Alta sector. Small mapped hollows and seasonal drainage remain part of the headward setting; no source-lake name is substituted for the unnamed upper reach.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper-valley tributary junction and transition to Arroyo Verde
correspondence.finding: The valley reaches the Manga Mocha–Luján sector. The mapped Arroyo de las Pinturas comes from the west, in the Laguna Honda sector, into this upper drainage. The selected southeastward continuation reaches the corridor labeled Arroyo Verde near La Chuchu and La Magdalena. This is a tributary/valley relationship, not permission to name the whole upper route after either downstream label.
correspondence.mapped_reach_name: Arroyo Verde in the mapped middle continuation; upper reach unnamed

correspondence.component_scope: Middle Arroyo Verde corridor
correspondence.finding: The named Arroyo Verde valley continues southeast past La Escondida and Las Merceditas, then east across the route58 corridor and south around the Cerro Ibáñez sector. Tributary channels join from the north and west. The original channel and valley depiction establishes this continuation independently of the retained model connectivity.

correspondence.component_scope: Laguna del Medio drainage relationship
correspondence.finding: East of Cerro Ibáñez, the Arroyo Verde corridor bends into the southern junction of the Laguna del Medio depression near El Águila, then leaves southeast toward Los Límites. The long northern lake/depression and its incoming drainage are separately visible. This reading supports a material basin-side junction, not a claim that the selected route crosses the entire northern lake or that the lake is named Arroyo Verde.
correspondence.mapped_reach_name: Arroyo Verde; Laguna del Medio remains a separate mapped feature

correspondence.component_scope: Lower border corridor and RN 3 crossing
correspondence.finding: The original map carries Arroyo Verde east through Los Límites, Aguada La Piedra, El Bagual and San Francisco to the RN 3 crossing at the Arroyo Verde locality. It then turns northeast through the Antorena sector. The flowline has repeated mapped Arroyo Verde labels on the actual corridor; the locality label alone is not the identification basis.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: East of the highway crossing the mapped Arroyo Verde channel trends northeast past El Miramar, crosses the coastal route and reaches the western shore of the Golfo San Matías north of Puerto Lobos. The coast, outlet channel and northward turn were read directly from the original map. Kokot’s coastal account independently distinguishes this mouth from Puerto Lobos and describes nearby coastal ridges among volcanic-rock exposures.

bounded_primary_prose.observation: The provincial Somuncurá management plan explicitly lists Arroyo Verde as an Atlantic-draining basin and distinguishes it from the separate Ventana–Los Berros–Salado system. This supports regional system context, not the exact selected connectors.

The coastal chapter describes the Arroyo Verde mouth and coastal-ridge deposits, placing Puerto Lobos farther south. Its editorial note states that the chapter’s references/data extend to2005; it is historical coastal context, not proof of present hydrological operation.
